finding: Low back pain in the past year (59.7%) was associated with chronic fatigue syndrome; shift work and occupation length were risk factors.
note: Not clinically diagnosed ME/CFS; abstract truncated

population: ME/CFS adolescents (broad case definition, broader than Fukuda)
finding: Twenty-seven plasma cytokines and network parameters did not differ between adolescent CFS patients and controls.
note: Broad definition without required accompanying symptoms; abstract truncated

finding: Exercise capacity (VO2peak) was significantly lower in CFS; in patients, higher VO2peak related to less daytime sleep; sleep latency and efficiency were normal but patients slept more and spent more time in bed.
77 serum cytokines separated ME (sensitivity 92.5%) and GWI (64.9%) from controls, top ones IL-7, IL-4, TNF-alpha, IL-13, IL-17F; GWI resembled controls more than ME did.
note: Small, no n in abstract; multiplex panel, no replication

finding: Analysis of Norwegian online ME forums identified four discursive domains sustaining a symbolic community.
No association between childhood trauma and 7-day salivary cortisol; emotional neglect was related negatively to a stress-reactivity measure (text truncated).
Systematic review of activity and participation instruments found limited psychometric evidence; CFS-APQ recommended.

CFS patients had worse symptoms, maximal voluntary contraction, muscle recovery and cognition than MS and controls; ME/Canadian criteria subgroups differed little, comorbid fibromyalgia added symptom burden.
Argues recovery thresholds for CFS should use normative data from healthy working-age people; PACE recovery definition may have overstated recovery.
Relaxation therapy: none of the studies reported autonomic outcomes; for CFS a multimodal approach seemed better than relaxation (3 studies).
CFS/ME participants had more post-traumatic stress symptoms and fewer coping strategies than controls; pain severity was not associated with trauma symptoms.
Patient attributions for global change ratings: improved patients cited behavioural changes, worsened cited stress.
Body awareness interventions improved FIQ, pain, depression, anxiety and quality of life, with high heterogeneity; mostly fibromyalgia.
note: Low quality evidence; few CFS studies

finding: Small left ventricle and low cardiac index (EDD <40 mm 45% vs 3%; cardiac index <2 53% vs 8%) were common in ME, and orthostatic intolerance was present in 35 of 36 tested.
note: Japanese cohort; ME diagnosis criteria not stated in abstract

finding: Sexual dysfunction was greater in women with CFS with more symptoms, fibromyalgia, Sjogren's or myofascial pain, and more fatigue.
ME International Consensus Criteria identified more impaired patients with more severe symptoms than Fukuda criteria.
Attention network test: error rates did not differ but information processing time was prolonged in CFS, most in complex conditions.
Medical students had limited knowledge of CFS and informal sources shaped attitudes.
